The brief contentions of the written statement of the respondent No.1 in both the petitions are as under:
The petitions are bad for non joinder of necessary parties i.e., Owner and Insurer of motor cycle bearing Rg.No.AP-03-KX-5844 are necessary party.

It has contended that the accident in question was occurred due to the sole negligence of the rider of motor cycle.
The rider and pillion rider were not wearing the helmet and violated the provisions of IMV Act.
The rider of motor cycle was not possessing valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident.
The owner of offending vehicle and concerned Police have not submitted details of accident to the office of this respondent.
Hence  SCCH-9 8 MVC.No.2854 & 2855/2021 they violated the provisions of IMV Act.
As such this respondent is not liable to pay the compensation.

In this context Ex.P6/hand sketch clearly goes to show that the accident was occurred on the extreme left side of the main road.
The Ex.P6 also goes to show that the place of accident is a zig-zag road and the driver of Bolero vehicle has taken the vehicle extreme left side of the road and caused the accident.
Apart from this the ExP5 Motor Vehicle Inspection report goes to show that there were damages almost front side of the offending vehicle.
There were no explain by the 1st respondent about these damages to the offending vehicle.
Therefore it appears that the said damages were caused due to accident between motorcycle and Bolero Vehicle.

As already stated above the charge sheet filed by the investigation officer also leveled charges against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence of rash and negligent and causing death of deceased.

Admittedly this RW.1 is not a eye witness to the accident.
Only on mere self swearing statement of RW1 cannot be held that there was no  SCCH-9 14 MVC.No.2854 & 2855/2021 negligence on the part of driver of Bolero vehicle.
This RW1 mainly contended that the rider of motor cycle was negligent in causing the accident.
For showing of this aspect, no document is placed before the Court.

Therefore, the evidence of RW1 is not sufficient to hold there was no negligence on the Koyyala Venkataramana vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52897701/

sentences.text: This RW1 also contended that the deceased were not wearing helmet hence violated the provisions of IMV Act and to consider contributory negligence.
However, showing this aspect also, this witness has not placed any document.
Moreover, the Investigating Officer has not charge sheeted against deceased persons for non wearing the helmet.
Therefore, the contentions of respondent No.1/RW1 that deceased persons were not wearing helmet at the time of accident cannot be sustainable.

17 . Moreover in a claim petition arising out of the accident the proving of negligence of offending vehicle is only preponderance of probabilities and not standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt as required in criminal case.
This principles of law was laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karanataka, in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (Civil) 319  SCCH-9 15 MVC.No.2854 & 2855/2021 (Kusum & Others V/s Satbir & others).

Therefore, the documents relied by the petitioners and oral evidence of PW1 & 2 clearly establishes that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligence act of the driver of the offending Bolero bearing Reg.No.No.AP-04-AK-7385.
Now it can safely be concluded, death was caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.
Therefore, I am of the opinion that the petitioners have proved issue No.1.

Hence, I answered issue No.1 in the affirmative in both Koyyala Venkataramana vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52897701/

Admittedly deceased was married and petitioners are husband and sons considered as the legal heir and dependents of the deceased.

In that sense, they were largely  dependent on the earnings of their mother and, in  fact, were staying with her, who met with an  accident at the young age of 48 years."
Therefore, in the instant case the petitioners are the husband and sons being legal representative are entitled for compensation.
Thus the above judgment is aptly applicable to present case on hand.
The Hon'ble Supreme court in Smt.Sarla Verma case, has held about deduction of salary based on number of family members.

In the instant case husband and major sons are dependents of deceased, hence 1/4th of the salary has to be deducted from the gross income of deceased towards her personal expenses and remaining is to be taken as dependency.
